items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: You didn't hear too much of him but you hear more about Professor than you hear about him.

ctx.x: Well there was a lot of that too going on. Yeah, well I mean he couldn't record on it so he, I think. How does a piano player like Professor Longhair fit into New Orleans? I mean where is his? He had his own style. He had his own

rhythmic thing that he did that's real funk and a lot of people just, it's just like the band today. They're playing ba ba da ba da, that type of thing you know, and they're playing a little faster than the older guys used to play. The Olympics, they're about the last of the old people that used to play, the stuff that they played. Because the bands, they were very together and they played a lot of harmony and a lot of stuff. A lot of bands they're doing that. But the Dirty Dozen came down with a lot of stuff,…
Yeah, he'd always sit down and, let me show you this. Yeah, let me show you this, let me show you that.
